title: Webb's book and the family band
summary: Webb's library of Dixon, Mundy, Redman and Sampson arrangements and his careful choice of men made the band, like Duke's, a family.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: lot of music. He had Charlie Dixon, he had Jimmy Mundy, Don Redman, Edgar Sampson and what came from other arrangers.
We'd buy arrangements from some guy who had arrangements on something, you know, we'd buy it. The guy write something special for us, you know.
Some other arrangers write different stuff never recorded, but we had a lot of music. A lot of pop stuff.
Melodies of waltzes, melodies of -- Like I say, we had tangos and Dr. Steele kept us up on -- he was a doctor of music. He'd make you play.
You had to play around him. People sitting in the band like Steel and Hilton Jefferson and those guys -- those were the top musicians.
You really got a chance -- When I went in the band, I found Jeff there, 'Oh, my goodness, Jeff's in there.' (Inaudible) with this guy -- beautiful.
